title: Chatter Retention Cohorts — D1 / D7 / D14 / D30
description: SQL-only cohort approximation: a chatter joins a channel cohort on their first observed local day inside the selected range, and retention means at least one message on the exact 1st, 7th, 14th, or 30th day afterward. Immature cohort percentages are left null; activity before the selected range is intentionally not used.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), activity AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    local_time::date AS activity_date
  FROM scoped
), cohorts AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_date) AS cohort_date
  FROM activity
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_id
), observed_bounds AS (
  SELECT MAX(activity_date) AS last_observed_date
  FROM activity
), retention AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel_name,
    c.cohort_date,
    c.user_id,
    BOOL_OR(a.activity_date = c.cohort_date + 1) AS retained_d1,
    BOOL_OR(a.activity_date = c.cohort_date + 7) AS retained_d7,
    BOOL_OR(a.activity_date = c.cohort_date + 14) AS retained_d14,
    BOOL_OR(a.activity_date = c.cohort_date + 30) AS retained_d30
  FROM cohorts c
  JOIN activity a
    ON a.channel_name = c.channel_name
   AND a.user_id = c.user_id
  GROUP BY c.channel_name, c.cohort_date, c.user_id
)
SELECT
  r.channel_name AS "Channel",
  r.cohort_date AS "Cohort",
  COUNT(*) AS "Cohort size",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 1 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d1) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D1 %",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 7 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d7) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D7 %",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 14 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d14) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D14 %",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 30 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d30) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D30 %"
FROM retention r
CROSS JOIN observed_bounds b
GROUP BY r.channel_name, r.cohort_date, b.last_observed_date
ORDER BY r.cohort_date DESC, r.channel_name

title: Channel Stickiness
description: SQL-only stickiness proxy: average daily unique chatters divided by all unique chatters observed for the channel in the selected range. This is a range-based DAU/audience ratio, not a true DAU/MAU metric unless the selected range is one month.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), daily AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    local_time::date AS local_day,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)::numeric AS daily_chatters
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY channel_name, local_time::date
), audiences AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)::numeric AS range_chatters
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY channel_name
)
SELECT
  d.channel_name AS "Channel",
  ROUND(100.0 * AVG(d.daily_chatters) / NULLIF(a.range_chatters, 0), 1) AS "Stickiness %"
FROM daily d
JOIN audiences a USING (channel_name)
GROUP BY d.channel_name, a.range_chatters
ORDER BY "Stickiness %" DESC, "Channel"

title: User Survival Curve / Activity Lifespan
description: SQL-only survival approximation: each chatter's lifespan is the number of local-calendar days between their first and last observed messages across the selected channels and time range. The curve is the share with an observed lifespan at least N days; it is right-censored, does not imply continuous activity, and is capped at 90 days.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), lifespans AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MAX(local_time::date) - MIN(local_time::date) AS lifespan_days
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY user_id
), day_numbers AS (
  SELECT GENERATE_SERIES(
    0,
    LEAST(COALESCE(MAX(lifespan_days), 0), 90)
  ) AS day_number
  FROM lifespans
)
SELECT
  day_number::text || 'd' AS "Observed lifespan",
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE l.lifespan_days >= d.day_number)
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
    1
  ) AS "Surviving %"
FROM day_numbers d
CROSS JOIN lifespans l
GROUP BY d.day_number
ORDER BY d.day_number

title: Subscriber Retention Proxy
description: SQL-only subscriber-retention proxy: a cohort starts on a chatter's first subscriber-tagged local day in the selected range, and retention requires another subscriber-tagged message exactly 7, 14, or 30 days later. Subscriber state is inferred from message fields, so silence is unknown rather than cancellation and immature percentages are null.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    subscriber_months > 0 OR subscription_tier > 0 AS is_subscriber
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), daily_status AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    local_time::date AS local_day,
    BOOL_OR(is_subscriber) AS is_subscriber
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_id, local_time::date
), subscriber_starts AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    MIN(local_day) FILTER (WHERE is_subscriber) AS cohort_date
  FROM daily_status
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_id
), cohorts AS (
  SELECT channel_name, user_id, cohort_date
  FROM subscriber_starts
  WHERE cohort_date IS NOT NULL
), observed_bounds AS (
  SELECT MAX(local_day) AS last_observed_date
  FROM daily_status
), retention AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel_name,
    c.cohort_date,
    c.user_id,
    BOOL_OR(d.local_day = c.cohort_date + 7 AND d.is_subscriber) AS retained_d7,
    BOOL_OR(d.local_day = c.cohort_date + 14 AND d.is_subscriber) AS retained_d14,
    BOOL_OR(d.local_day = c.cohort_date + 30 AND d.is_subscriber) AS retained_d30
  FROM cohorts c
  JOIN daily_status d
    ON d.channel_name = c.channel_name
   AND d.user_id = c.user_id
  GROUP BY c.channel_name, c.cohort_date, c.user_id
)
SELECT
  r.channel_name AS "Channel",
  r.cohort_date AS "Cohort",
  COUNT(*) AS "Subscribers",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 7 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d7) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D7 %",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 14 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d14) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D14 %",
  CASE WHEN r.cohort_date + 30 <= b.last_observed_date
    THEN ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.retained_d30) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 1)
  END AS "D30 %"
FROM retention r
CROSS JOIN observed_bounds b
GROUP BY r.channel_name, r.cohort_date, b.last_observed_date
ORDER BY r.cohort_date DESC, r.channel_name

title: Community Turnover
description: SQL-only turnover approximation: for each local-calendar day after the first, turnover is 100 × (arrivals + departures) / the union of chatter IDs active that day or the prior day. Empty calendar days inside the selected range are included; identities without user_id are excluded.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), activity AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    channel_name,
    local_time::date AS local_day,
    user_id
  FROM scoped
), bounds AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    MIN(local_day) AS first_day,
    MAX(local_day) AS last_day
  FROM activity
  GROUP BY channel_name
), calendar AS (
  SELECT
    b.channel_name,
    day_value::date AS local_day
  FROM bounds b
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL GENERATE_SERIES(
    b.first_day::timestamp,
    b.last_day::timestamp,
    INTERVAL '1 day'
  ) AS day_value
  WHERE day_value::date > b.first_day
), membership AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel_name,
    c.local_day,
    current_day.user_id,
    TRUE AS active_now,
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM activity previous_day
      WHERE previous_day.channel_name = c.channel_name
        AND previous_day.local_day = c.local_day - 1
        AND previous_day.user_id = current_day.user_id
    ) AS active_before
  FROM calendar c
  JOIN activity current_day
    ON current_day.channel_name = c.channel_name
   AND current_day.local_day = c.local_day

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    c.channel_name,
    c.local_day,
    previous_day.user_id,
    FALSE AS active_now,
    TRUE AS active_before
  FROM calendar c
  JOIN activity previous_day
    ON previous_day.channel_name = c.channel_name
   AND previous_day.local_day = c.local_day - 1
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM activity current_day
    WHERE current_day.channel_name = c.channel_name
      AND current_day.local_day = c.local_day
      AND current_day.user_id = previous_day.user_id
  )
)
SELECT
  m.local_day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS time,
  m.channel_name AS metric,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE m.active_now <> m.active_before)
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0),
    1
  ) AS value
FROM membership m
GROUP BY m.channel_name, m.local_day
ORDER BY time, metric

title: First-Time vs Returning Chatters by Channel
description: SQL-only classification approximation using stored history: first-time means the chatter's first-ever stored message for that channel falls inside the selected time range; returning means an earlier stored channel message exists. Users without user_id are excluded, and missing history can overstate first-time chatters.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), active_chatters AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT channel_name, user_id
  FROM scoped
), selected_bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(event_time) AS first_event, MAX(event_time) AS last_event
  FROM scoped
), first_seen AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    MIN(event_time) AS first_event
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_id
)
SELECT
  a.channel_name AS "Channel",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE f.first_event >= b.first_event
      AND f.first_event <= b.last_event
  ) AS "First-time",
  COUNT(*) FILTER (
    WHERE f.first_event < b.first_event
  ) AS "Returning"
FROM active_chatters a
JOIN first_seen f USING (channel_name, user_id)
CROSS JOIN selected_bounds b
GROUP BY a.channel_name
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, a.channel_name

title: Dormant Chatter Reactivation
description: SQL-only reactivation proxy: a chatter is reactivated on the first stored message after a gap of at least 30 × 24 hours from their previous stored message in the same channel. The chart counts distinct reactivated chatters per local day; incomplete history can miss or misclassify gaps.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), candidate_chatters AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT channel_name, user_id
  FROM scoped
), selected_bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(event_time) AS first_event, MAX(event_time) AS last_event
  FROM scoped
), ordered_history AS (
  SELECT
    e.event_time,
    e.channel_name,
    e.user_id,
    LAG(e.event_time) OVER (
      PARTITION BY e.channel_name, e.user_id
      ORDER BY e.event_time, e.id NULLS LAST, e.message_id NULLS LAST
    ) AS previous_event
  FROM twitch_event_chat e
  JOIN candidate_chatters c
    ON c.channel_name = e.channel_name
   AND c.user_id = e.user_id
  CROSS JOIN selected_bounds b
  WHERE e.event_time <= b.last_event
), reactivations AS (
  SELECT
    h.event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    h.channel_name,
    h.user_id
  FROM ordered_history h
  CROSS JOIN selected_bounds b
  WHERE h.event_time >= b.first_event
    AND h.event_time <= b.last_event
    AND h.previous_event IS NOT NULL
    AND h.event_time - h.previous_event >= INTERVAL '30 days'
)
SELECT
  local_time::date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS time,
  channel_name AS metric,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS value
FROM reactivations
GROUP BY channel_name, local_time::date
ORDER BY time, metric

title: Subscriber Tier Transitions
description: SQL-only transition approximation: each chatter-channel-day is assigned the maximum subscription_tier observed in messages, then consecutive observed active days are compared. Rows count observed tier changes, not billing events; inactive days and message-level badge inconsistencies are not interpreted as cancellations.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    subscription_tier
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), daily_tier AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    local_time::date AS local_day,
    MAX(subscription_tier) AS tier
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY channel_name, user_id, local_time::date
), ordered_tiers AS (
  SELECT
    channel_name,
    user_id,
    local_day,
    tier,
    LAG(tier) OVER (
      PARTITION BY channel_name, user_id
      ORDER BY local_day
    ) AS previous_tier
  FROM daily_tier
), transitions AS (
  SELECT channel_name, user_id, previous_tier, tier
  FROM ordered_tiers
  WHERE previous_tier IS NOT NULL
    AND previous_tier <> tier
)
SELECT
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  CASE previous_tier
    WHEN 0 THEN 'Non-subscriber'
    WHEN 1 THEN 'Tier 1'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'Tier 2'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'Tier 3'
    ELSE 'Tier ' || previous_tier::text
  END AS "From",
  CASE tier
    WHEN 0 THEN 'Non-subscriber'
    WHEN 1 THEN 'Tier 1'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'Tier 2'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'Tier 3'
    ELSE 'Tier ' || tier::text
  END AS "To",
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS "Chatters",
  COUNT(*) AS "Transitions"
FROM transitions
GROUP BY channel_name, previous_tier, tier
ORDER BY "Transitions" DESC, "Channel", previous_tier, tier

title: Channel Affinity Score
description: SQL-only affinity approximation: for every chatter, calculate the percentage of their selected-range messages across the selected channels that went to each channel, then average those percentages per channel. A score of 100% means the channel's observed chatters were exclusive to it within the current selection.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT channel_name, user_id
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), channel_messages AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    channel_name,
    COUNT(*)::numeric AS messages
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY user_id, channel_name
), user_totals AS (
  SELECT user_id, SUM(messages) AS total_messages
  FROM channel_messages
  GROUP BY user_id
), affinity AS (
  SELECT
    c.channel_name,
    c.user_id,
    100.0 * c.messages / NULLIF(t.total_messages, 0) AS affinity_score
  FROM channel_messages c
  JOIN user_totals t USING (user_id)
)
SELECT
  channel_name AS "Channel",
  ROUND(AVG(affinity_score), 1) AS "Affinity %"
FROM affinity
GROUP BY channel_name
ORDER BY "Affinity %" DESC, "Channel"

title: Audience Composition Drift
description: SQL-only composition approximation: each local-day chatter across the selected channels is classified once as first-time, returning subscriber, or returning non-subscriber. First-time uses earliest stored activity in the selected-channel universe; subscriber status is inferred from that day's messages, and each series is its daily share of observed chatters.

targets.rawSql:
WITH scoped AS (
  SELECT
    event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS local_time,
    user_id,
    subscriber_months,
    subscription_tier
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE $__timeFilter(event_time)
    AND channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
), daily_chatters AS (
  SELECT
    local_time::date AS local_day,
    user_id,
    BOOL_OR(subscriber_months > 0 OR subscription_tier > 0) AS is_subscriber
  FROM scoped
  GROUP BY local_time::date, user_id
), first_seen AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(event_time AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}')::date AS first_local_day
  FROM twitch_event_chat
  WHERE channel_name IN (${channel:sqlstring})
    AND user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY user_id
), classified AS (
  SELECT
    d.local_day,
    d.user_id,
    CASE
      WHEN f.first_local_day = d.local_day THEN 'First-time'
      WHEN d.is_subscriber THEN 'Returning subscriber'
      ELSE 'Returning non-subscriber'
    END AS segment
  FROM daily_chatters d
  JOIN first_seen f USING (user_id)
), segment_counts AS (
  SELECT local_day, segment, COUNT(*)::numeric AS chatters
  FROM classified
  GROUP BY local_day, segment
)
SELECT
  local_day::timestamp AT TIME ZONE '${timezone}' AS time,
  segment AS metric,
  ROUND(
    100.0 * chatters / NULLIF(SUM(chatters) OVER (PARTITION BY local_day), 0),
    1
  ) AS value
FROM segment_counts
ORDER BY time, metric
